headline_marked: [[Meta to use custom AMD Instinct MI400 accelerators]] with 144GB HBM4, report claims
headline: Meta to use custom AMD Instinct MI400 accelerators with 144GB HBM4, report claims
summary: The custom MI400s will have significantly less memory than standard models, optimized for recommendation systems to dramatically cut costs, but at the expense of versatility for frontier AI models.
details: Meta's custom AMD Instinct MI450-based AI accelerator will reportedly use 144GB of HBM4 memory, a third of the full-blown MI455X's 432GB. These specialized chips are optimized primarily for recommendation systems on Facebook and other social platforms.

The reduction in HBM4 capacity and compute performance is expected to dramatically lower the bill of materials, as HBM4 is exceptionally expensive. This custom design could potentially save Meta tens of millions of dollars by reducing costs and package size.

As added benefits, these custom MI450-series accelerators will also consume significantly less power when running recommendation workloads without a major reduction in performance. This could lead to a substantially better total-cost-of-ownership for their intended use.

However, this specialization comes with a significant disadvantage: a loss of versatility. The reduced compute and HBM make them less attractive for large language model (LLM) training and inference, potentially restricting modern AI workloads.

Unlike general-purpose Instinct MI455X chips that can be reassigned, Meta's specialized version is less flexible outside its intended workload. If Meta's compute demand shifts towards model training and LLM inference, they might find their installed base of accelerators unsuitable.

This situation could force Meta's frontier AI division to purchase more general-purpose accelerators, potentially from Nvidia or full-fat AMD Instinct MI455X systems. This creates an irony where cost-saving specialization could lead to increased spending on other hardware.

AMD and Meta previously confirmed an agreement for 6 GW of Instinct AI accelerators over five years, including custom MI450 designs. It now appears these custom units are intended only for select workloads, rather than a broad range of AI tasks.
